title: Grandpa's notes

caption:
Part 3. Grandpa left one rule in his notebook. 📓

Original fiction. Part 4 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: Lena stopped a fire the radio predicted, and the next broadcast said her name.
scenes.image: the old walnut radio glowing on a kitchen table at night, a woman's silhouette in the doorway

scenes.narration: It never said what the cost was. It just went back to the weather. Clear skies. Below zero. Then static.
scenes.image: frost creeping across a dark kitchen window, the amber glow of a radio reflected in the glass

scenes.narration: So she tore apart her grandfather's workshop. Spools of copper wire. Burnt-out tubes. A coffee can full of keys to nothing.
scenes.image: cluttered basement workshop lit by a single hanging bulb, copper wire spools and old vacuum tubes on a workbench

scenes.narration: Behind the furnace, wrapped in oilcloth, she found his notebook.
scenes.image: a woman's hands unwrapping a worn leather notebook from oilcloth in a dim basement

scenes.narration: Fifty years of entries. Every broadcast he'd heard. Everything he'd changed. And a tick mark beside what happened next.
scenes.image: old notebook pages covered in faded illegible pencil scrawl, out of focus, lamplight

scenes.narration: Winter, 1971. He kept a man off the quarry ice. Three days later, the man's brother went through it instead.
scenes.image: a frozen quarry at dusk surrounded by bare trees, a dark crack across the ice

scenes.narration: Spring, 1983. He warned a neighbor about a gas leak. The leak happened anyway. Two streets over. To strangers.
scenes.image: a quiet suburban street at night, one house's windows glowing orange in the distance

scenes.narration: The last page was underlined twice. Never change more than one thing. It always balances. One for one.
scenes.image: an old fountain pen resting across an open notebook on a workbench, lamplight, shadows

scenes.narration: Lena counted. She had changed only one thing. The fire. Just one. She let herself breathe.
scenes.image: woman sitting on basement stairs clutching a leather notebook to her chest, eyes closed in relief

scenes.narration: Then, upstairs, the radio switched itself on. It was noon. In fifty years, it had never played at noon. Special bulletin, said the voice. The balance comes due on Friday.
scenes.image: the old radio glowing in an empty daylit kitchen, pale winter sun through the window, dust in the air
